summary: A pre-launch page for a product (or event) that is not live yet: one promise, one validated email form, a countdown to the opening, a few proof points and a 'you're on the list' state with a referral link that moves the person up the line.

pages.purpose: One page with one job: get the visitor's email for the launch, with enough proof that it is worth it.

sections.purpose: One-line promise and the email form in a card over a soft photo, with the countdown to the first wave.
fields: Launch / first-wave date and time with time zone
What happens after sign-up (when they hear from you)
sections.notes: The only form on the page: email validated on submit, then live once it has been wrong, error tied to the input; on success a toast and the joined state. Wash the photo so text sits on calm ground. Countdown renders placeholders on the server, ticks after hydration, hides the digits from screen readers and reads one sentence with the day count; honour reduced motion. EmailCapture gives the validated field, consent line and success state with the same server contract as ContactForm.

sections.purpose: Three proof points: what the product does, each with a figure.
alternatives: stats-band: when the proof points are mainly numbers
fields: Per point: figure, title, one sentence

sections.purpose: When it launches, what it costs, which platforms, what happens to the email.

pages.purpose: Confirmation after sign-up: the person's place in line, a share link that moves them up, and what happens next.

sections.purpose: Place in line counting in after sign-up; each friend who joins with the link moves them up a fixed number of places, with a progress bar to the first wave.
alternatives: stat: the position as a plain figure with progress, when the layout needs its own design
empty-state: a plain confirmation when there is no referral programme
fields: Queue position logic (start position, places gained per referral)
What the person gets at the front
sections.notes: Counter eases to the new number (instant under reduced motion) and is announced via aria-live. Without a referral programme show a plain confirmation instead. ReferralPanel takes the position, the real total, referrals and the goal; the app owns the rules.

sections.purpose: Personal invite link with a copy button and share options.
alternatives: qr-code: when the link is shared in person
input: a read-only link field with a copy button, when the share row stands alone
sections.notes: Copy result announced with a toast. ReferralPanel includes the read-only link, copy (announced) and the device share sheet where there is one.

sections.purpose: What happens next and when the next email arrives.
alternatives: cta: a single line with a link back to the home page

content: Launch or first-wave date, time and time zone
Email provider / list where sign-ups go, with double opt-in
Consent text and what will be sent
Referral rules (places per referral, first-wave size) if used
FAQ answers: price, platforms, timing, data use

styles.name: soft editorial glass
styles.why: Consumer products before launch: a soft photo, a serif headline cut in, digits that rise into place; unhurried.

styles.name: dark launch countdown
styles.why: Tech launches and events: dark with one hot accent so the countdown and form are all that stand out.

pitfalls: A countdown that reaches zero with nothing live; update the page or switch it to 'out now' before the date.
Countdowns without a time zone, or that cause hydration mismatches and read every second to screen readers.
Collecting emails without consent text, double opt-in or a privacy link.
Fake waiting-list numbers or positions; only show counts that are real.
Validation errors not tied to the input, or an error shown before the person typed anything.
More than one call to action; the page has one job.
Referral schemes that promise rewards the business cannot deliver at launch.
